description: A version is proposed only once it has been public for seven days, so that a release pulled or fixed in its first week never reaches a branch. internalChecksFilter is already strict by default; it is stated so that the wait is read here as holding back the branch and the pull request themselves, not only a status check on them

packageRules.description: The base image is pinned to a digest, so that a rebuild of the same tag upstream reaches the image through a pull request whose build has passed, and the weekly release publishes it as a new version. Pinning is limited to the Dockerfile; actions keep their version tags

The base image is proposed without the seven-day wait. Docker Hub gives a tag's last push as its release time, and the official ubuntu tags are pushed again every day or two, so a tag never looks seven days old and no update would ever be proposed. The pull request's build still has to pass

Patch releases, digest updates and the first pins are merged by Renovate itself once the pull request's checks have passed. Renovate merges rather than the platform, so that the repository needs no auto-merge setting or branch protection; a pull request with no checks is never merged. Minor and major updates open a pull request to be reviewed by hand

Workflows are already read by the github-actions manager. Grouping them keeps a handful of actions from arriving as a handful of pull requests, since they are updated together and reviewed the same way
